#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Append one provisioning entry to the users configuration.

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
readonly ROOT

# shellcheck source=lib/format.sh
source "${ROOT}/lib/format.sh"

name=''
login_shell='/bin/bash'
out="${ROOT}/config/users.conf"

while (($# > 0)); do
  case "$1" in
    --name)
      name="${2:-}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --shell)
      login_shell="${2:-}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --out)
      out="${2:-}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    *)
      printf 'unknown option: %s\n' "$1" >&2
      exit 64
      ;;
  esac
done

mkdir -p -- "$(dirname -- "${out}")"
format_line "${name}" "${login_shell}" >> "${out}"
printf 'wrote %s for %s\n' "${out}" "${name}"

.PHONY: test

test:
	@find . -name '*_test.sh' -print0 | xargs -0 -r -n1 bash
# Formatting helpers for the provisioning configuration.
# shellcheck shell=bash

# Formats one users.conf entry.
# Arguments: account name, login shell
# Outputs: the formatted line on stdout
format_line() {
  printf '%s:%s\n' "$1" "$2"
}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Coverage for lib/format.sh.

set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
readonly ROOT

# shellcheck source=lib/format.sh
source "${ROOT}/lib/format.sh"

result="$(format_line alice /bin/bash)"
if [[ ${result} != 'alice:/bin/bash' ]]; then
  printf 'format_line returned %s\n' "${result}" >&2
  exit 1
fi

printf 'ok lib/format.sh\n'
root:/bin/bash

python3 - <<'E'
p='bin/mkuser-config.sh'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''mkdir -p --''','''if [[ -z ${name} ]]; then
  printf 'error: --name must not be empty\\n' >&2
  exit 64
fi

mkdir -p --''',1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
cat > bin/mkuser-config_test.sh <<'E'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Coverage for bin/mkuser-config.sh.

set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
readonly ROOT
script="${ROOT}/bin/mkuser-config.sh"

tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf -- "${tmp}"' EXIT
out="${tmp}/users.conf"

fail() {
  printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$1" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Empty name, and missing --name, are rejected without writing anything.
for args in '--name ""' ''; do
  eval "bash \"${script}\" ${args} --out \"${out}\"" 2>"${tmp}/err" >/dev/null
  status=$?
  ((status != 0)) || fail "empty name (${args}) exited 0"
  grep -q -- '--name must not be empty' "${tmp}/err" || fail "no message for (${args})"
  [[ ! -s ${out} ]] || fail "config written for (${args})"
done

# A valid name still works.
bash "${script}" --name bob --out "${out}" >/dev/null || fail 'valid name rejected'
[[ $(cat "${out}") == 'bob:/bin/bash' ]] || fail 'valid entry wrong'

printf 'ok bin/mkuser-config.sh\n'
E
make test

`bin/mkuser-config.sh` now rejects an empty or missing `--name`. It prints `error: --name must not be empty` to stderr, exits 64 (matching the script's existing usage-error code) and writes nothing. `make test` passes.

The new test is `bin/mkuser-config_test.sh`, which `make test` picks up automatically. It covers `--name ""`, a missing `--name` and a valid name (`bob`). For the two rejected cases it checks the non-zero exit, the message, and that the output file is still empty.

I didn't confirm that the test fails without the fix. I haven't committed anything.
